nodes.summary: For an alphabet $T$, write $T \sqcup T$ for the disjoint union of a left and a right copy of $T$. This is the deterministic automaton over $T \sqcup T$ with the two states true and false, whose start state and only accepting state are true, and which moves from state $b$ on a letter $c$ to true exactly when $b$ is true and $c$ lies in the left copy, and to false otherwise.
nodes.title: Automaton for words over the left copy

nodes.summary: The left quotient of a context-free language by a regular language is context-free, over a finite alphabet.
nodes.title: The left quotient of a context-free language by a regular language is context-free

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $T$, write $T \sqcup T$ for the disjoint union of a left and a right copy of $T$. This is the language over $T \sqcup T$ of the words obtained from a word $x$ over $T$ by replacing each letter with its left copy.
nodes.title: Words over the left copy of a doubled alphabet

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a deterministic automaton over an alphabet $T$, and write $T \sqcup T$ for the disjoint union of a left and a right copy of $T$. This is the deterministic automaton over $T \sqcup T$ whose states are the states of $D$ together with one extra dead state $\bot$. From a state $p$ of $D$, on the right copy of a letter $a$ it moves to the state that $D$ reaches from $p$ on $a$; on a letter of the left copy,…
nodes.title: Automaton running a deterministic automaton on the right copy

nodes.summary: The right quotient of a context-free language by a regular language is context-free, over a finite alphabet.
nodes.title: The right quotient of a context-free language by a regular language is context-free

nodes.summary: For languages $L$ and $R$ over an alphabet $T$, the right quotient of $L$ by $R$ is the language of all words $x$ over $T$ such that the concatenation $xy$ lies in $L$ for some word $y \in R$.
nodes.title: Right quotient of a language by a language

nodes.summary: For a language $R$ over an alphabet $T$, write $T \sqcup T$ for the disjoint union of a left and a right copy of $T$. This is the language over $T \sqcup T$ of the words obtained from a word $y \in R$ by replacing each letter with its right copy.
nodes.title: Words of a language marked by the right copy

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $T$, write $T \sqcup T$ for the disjoint union of a left and a right copy of $T$. This map sends the left copy and the right copy of a letter $a \in T$ to the one-letter word $a$ over $T$.
nodes.title: Forgetting the copy of a letter

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
